Subject: Hosted API: increased p95 due to KV sync backlog — initial notice

Hi Seth / Brightline ops team,

Quick note to let you know we're seeing elevated p95 generation latency for a subset of your requests starting ~2027-08-09 14:50 UTC. Symptoms:
- P95 token-generation latency increased from ~350ms to ~1.6s for a small percentage of sessions (traffic hitting prefix groups A12-A18).
- No increase in 5xx error rate; most requests complete slower.
- Affected paths are primarily streaming chat and multi-turn sessions that rely on KV lookups.

What we're doing now:
- Flagged an incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-08-09-kv-sync (link below).
- Added a temporary read-path fallback to primary store for impacted prefixes to reduce tail latency.
- Increasing replication worker concurrency and pausing scheduled background compaction while we investigate.

Attachments: kv_sync_diagnostic_20270809.txt (mini-dump with sample request IDs and timing).

Could you confirm if you see any user-facing errors on your side or increased retry attempts? Any recent workload changes on your end (bursting, long-running batch jobs) would be useful context.

I'll loop in engineering and CS. ETA update in ~30–60m.

Priya / team — quick engineering update from the bridge:

Root cause (preliminary):
- A scheduled metadata compaction job overlapped with a traffic spike that produced high write amplification on our KV replication queue.
- Replication worker threads were saturated; the queue backlog led to increased prefix-miss rates and synchronous read-throughs for certain routing keys (A12-A18).

Immediate mitigation applied (15:35–15:50 UTC):
- Paused the compaction job to reduce write amplification.
- Increased replication worker concurrency by +50% and temporarily raised replication commit batching to reduce per-write overhead.
- Enabled read-path fallback for the affected prefixes (serves from primary) to avoid blocked replica reads.

Result: p95 has dropped from ~1.6s to ~420ms in our sampled traces; average is stable. We're still monitoring for any regression during the next 60–90 minutes.

Next steps / permanent fix candidates:
1) Add backpressure on compaction when replication backlog > threshold.
2) Rate-limit certain background jobs during production traffic peaks.
3) Add more granular prefetching for high-cardinality prefixes to reduce synchronous misses.
4) Post-incident: tuning of replication batch sizes and a regression test to simulate compaction + spike.

Attachments: replay_segments.tar.gz (compressed sample of replication segments for offline analysis).

ETA: expect stable behaviour by 17:00 UTC; will provide a follow-up message when the incident is closed and then book a postmortem invite for next week.

Lauren Bishop

Hi Seth — following up with final status and next steps.

Status:
- We observed service performance return to normal by 2027-08-10 09:12 UTC after the mitigations described below.
- There were no customer-visible data drops or corrupted responses; all requests completed.

What caused it:
- A background compaction job that overlapped with a traffic spike created replication queue backlog and increased prefix-miss synchronous read-throughs.

What we did:
- Paused compaction, increased replication worker concurrency, enabled read fallback for affected prefixes.
- These mitigations reduced tail latency; further permanent fixes are planned (backpressure, rate limits, test harness).

Artifacts and next steps:
- Incident record / timeline: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-08-09-kv-sync
- Diagnostic dump and sample replication segments: kv_sync_diagnostic_20270809.txt, replay_segments.tar.gz (attached).

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the formal postmortem and a proposed timeline for fixes. Please let me know if you'd like a deeper call before the postmortem.
